lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ana Luiza Sellmann | Lesson 7 -- The Way It Used To Be

listenings.text: You are going to laugh at this one. When you were small you used to hide behind the sofa every time somebody rang the doorbell. Every time. And you did not use to eat anything green, not one single thing, which is funny now because you eat everything. Your brother used to copy you in absolutely everything, so for about two years he hid behind the sofa too. We used to walk to the bakery every Saturday morning, the three of us, and you always used to ask for the same bread. Nowadays nobody walks anywhere in that street. Anyway, I found the photos. I will send them tonight.

You asked me what it used to be like, so here it is. When I started, we did not use to work with any of this. There was no shared folder. Everything went to the client on paper and, if they wanted a change, somebody used to drive across the city with a new version in a bag. We used to spend three days on one presentation. In-house teams did everything, and a freelancer was somebody you called in an emergency. Nowadays it is the opposite, and honestly I think it is better, although I do miss the part where the work stopped when you left the building.

extra_audio.text: Victor recognises Ana in the old street and says she used to be much smaller. Ana answers that the whole street used to look bigger to her. Victor explains that there used to be a bakery on the corner where the bank is now. Ana asks him whether he still lives in the same building. Victor says that he does, and that he did not use to imagine staying for thirty years.
